source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text: Because a pre-mixed 13-13-21 NPK fertilizer formula is not readily available for purchase in Cambodia, farmers in this program were trained to mix their own equivalent blend from three fertilizers that are available: DAP (diammonium phosphate, 18-46-0), urea (46-0-0), and a potassium fertilizer (0-0-60, i.e. muriate of potash). Combining these three in the right proportions produces a blend that approximates a 13-13-21 N-P-K ratio, which is the formula used for the pre-harvest fertilizer application (see the fruiting-stage fertilizer schedule). This mixing method was demonstrated to farmers directly, over about 20 training/demonstration sessions.
